Abraham complains about an outstanding debt owed by the recipient, and the recipient’s stinginess toward the descendants of his former teacher. Signed Abraham Sagis. Verso: Part of an address. C. late 16th century. (Information from CUDL)
Document - needs examination.
Informal note addressed to Abū l-Afrāḥ ʿArūs b. Yosef about a business matter. Reused on verso by ʿArūs for accounts.
List of names and items in Arabic on a bifolio, such as carpets (بساطين) and sea shell (صدفة). Medieval-era. Requires further examination.

Recto (reuse): Official receipt for [...] b. ʿAlī, mentioning the kharāj and a waterwheel (sāqiya). The payment was 1 dinar. The entire date is difficult to read, but the year seems like 517 H.

Verso (original use): Fragment of a legal document in Arabic script. Needs examination.

Long piece from a deed of sale of an enslaved woman. Abū l-Faraj Yeshuʿa ha-Levi sells an enslaved person named Jaḥūn(?) to Abū l-Riḍā. In the hand of the scribe Ḥalfon b. Menashshe (1100-1138 CE). (Information from CUDL)
Deed regarding the endowment of a small house in Fusṭāṭ, mentioning the Babylonian synagogue. Ca. 11th-12th century. (Information from CUDL)

tags: account, commercial receipt, Arus b. Yosef
desc:
Commercial receipt for Abū l-Afrāḥ ʿArūs (b. Yūsuf) al-Urjuwānī, with Judaeo-Arabic business accounts in his own hand on verso. The set of similar documents:
ENA 3957.5
T-S Ar.35.128
T-S Ar.35.269
T-S Ar.39.187
T-S AS 184.265
ENA 3957.11 (for Nahray b. Nissim; all the rest are for ʿArūs)
Folio 1: Haggada. Folio 2: The book of Numbers, including its conclusion and verse count, followed by a note in Judaeo-Arabic that mentions "the Tāj that is in the Palestinian synagogue in Fustat."

List of names followed by numbers, possibly contributions to the poor. May be related to T-S AS 202.369. Mentions Ṣedaqa; Ibn Saʿīd al-[...]; the boys (ṣibyān) of al-[...]; the garment makers (al-thawwābīn); the servants (ghilmān) of the amīr; something in the sūq al-kabīr.
Small fragment from a ketubba. (Information from CUDL)

tags: Evyatar b. Eliyyahu, communal, book trade, colophon
desc: Colophon in the handwriting of Evyatar Ha-Kohen b. Eliyyahu Gaon.
Verso: Arabic document. Accounts or order of payment? Mentions Abū Naṣr. Recto is filled with strings of alefs, circles, and vertical lines.

Unidentified document in Arabic script. Upper right corner. Moderately wide spacing between the lines. Might be legal or a letter (may begin with the word "yaḥḍur"). A piece of cloth (related to T-S AS 176.43) is stuck to the back.
Letter(s). Recto and verso are in different hands and orientations. Verso contains phrases typical of letters of appeal for charity.

Legal document. Fragment (bottom part only). In the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe. Dated: 1435 Seleucid, which is 1123/24 CE. None of the substance of the case is preserved. Two copies of this document were made. (Information in part from CUDL)

Letter from Marduk b. Musa, Alexandria, to Nahray b. Nissim, Fustat, about a shipment of yarn from Fustat to Alexandria. Marduk notes that a baqyar (large-sized turban) 25 cubits long was made for Nahray, along with a bolt of cloth 20 cubits long. He further reports that ‘Atiyya b. Shammāʿ brought him a blue kerchief containing cotton, [linen] yarn and unraveled flax, which would be combined with yarn previously sent — and currently in the hands of the artisan — to produce another cloth, but that since the yarns were of different qualities, it didn't bleach well. The letter reveals the importa
Legal query, addressed to Moses Maimonides. Dating: ca. 1168–1204 CE, based on the years when he was active in Egypt. (Information from CUDL)
Printed treatise in Ladino and Hebrew. Translation of Mishna Avot.
Small fragment of an official (state-related) letter of praise/recommendation for somebody. Two lines are preserved.
Upper part of a letter in Judaeo-Arabic addressed to 'the brother R. Avraham.' The sender is in difficult straits. Mentions wheat on the roof.

Official letter in Arabic script. The sender received a letter from ʿAlī b. Aḥmad Ibn al-Aysar delivered by the ghulām of one of the Baghdādī merchants. Mentions someone who is traveling to ʿIrāq. In between the lines, a scribe-in-training has recopied the lines. On recto there is piyyuṭ. (Information in part from CUDL)
Late letter, apparently written by a certain Dhārā (?). The marginal section mentions "trousers for children" and something carried or delivered by a certain Meʾīr. (Information partly from CUDL)
Letter fragment. In Judaeo-Arabic. Addressed to 'mawlāy al-dayyān Abū [...].' Mentions Fustat and selling something.

tags: tax, Petition, Coptic numerals, tawqi', Saladin, calendar
desc: Petition to Saladin from ʿAbd al-Bāqī b. Yaḥyā, the Jew, a resident of Malīj, in the province of al-Gharbiyya, in the Delta. Dating: ca. 564–89 AH, which is 1169–93 CE. The petitioner complains about the tax collectors, who forced him to leave his family and job and to work for them, and asks for the issuing of a rescript that would allow him to go back to his town and family. On verso is an answer to the petition maintaining that since ʿAbd al-Bāqī b. Yaḥyā had some experience as a tax collector, he could not avoid this service. Also on verso is a work on calendar reckoning mentioning the maḥ

Fragment from the lower right corner of an agreement between a husband, Abū ʿAlī Yefet b. Yeshuʿa ha-Kohen, and wife, Sitt al-Ḍiyāʾ. The text is fragmentary but is seems that the husband takes upon himself to travel before he will have a child. Written by Halfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi (fl. 1100–1138 CE) under the authority of Masliah Gaon (r. 1127–1139). Dating: 1127–38 CE.

Marriage contract. Location: Cairo. Date is missing. Groom: Natan ha-Kohen b. Shela ha-Zaqen. The trousseau list may be found in ll. 6–13. (Information from Goitein notes and index card linked below.) On verso there are jottings of Hebrew literary text.
Letter from Salah b. Barhun al-Taharti to Yosef b. Awkal and his sons Hillel and Binyamin (written 8.21.1008, received 11.1.1008), upper fragment only.

Small fragment from the bottom of a legal document with wide line spacing. On parchment. A ketubba? Dating: ca. early 12th century. The document is signed by [... b. Ghā]lib ha-Ḥazzan. The validation is signed by Yiṣḥaq b. Shemuel ha-Sefaradi.

Report from a Fatimid chancery clerk concerning an iqṭāʿ. The land is a sugarcane plantation (al-qand), mentions dīwān al-qand, or rather dīwān al-saʿīd, and the names of at least three officials. Overall, the document records the submission and receipt of fiscal revenues from the rural district of Minyat Sandabasṭ al-Qadīma in Egypt. The document concerns the delivery of two current instalments owed to the dīwān, representing assessed revenues associated with local wells or irrigation resources (abyār) that had been granted as iqṭāʿ holdings. The payment pertains to the fiscal year 520 H, whi

Letter from Judge Eliyyahu to his colleague David ha-Kohen in Bilbays addressing a query; asks whether one Bushr, daughter of Asad, had formally dissolved a previous engagement and is free to remarry.

Recto: liturgical composition, followed by a genealogical list, starting with the Nasi Sar Shalom and going back seven generations (Sar Shalom b. Pinḥas b. Hodaya b. Yoshiyyahu b. Yehuda b. Shelomo b. ʿUziyyahu b. Yoshiyyahu). (Information from CUDL and Goitein's index card.) See Mann, Jews, II, p. 208. See also T-S 13J25.21.

Fragment from the top of a legal document mainly in Judaeo-Arabic. On parchment. Yosef b. Sh[...] appears before the court. Mentions the sage Netanʾel (החכם ה . . . השר הגדול . . . [המ]עולה מרנא ורבנא נתנאל); someone [ha-Levi] (whose name is followed by the abbreviation נר - "may the merciful one preserve him") and the number 40.
Cheque signed by Abū Zikrī Kohen (to be added to the list of checks in India Book 5). Khalīl is to give the bearer 3 ounces of soap. AA

Rhymed invitation to a festive event on the 29th of the month at 3:00 at the home of Nissim Lumbroso (נסים לומברוזו). Dating: 19th century. The invitation is copied out two and a half times, so probably this is merely a writing exercise.

Verso: Contributors list? Abū Sahl: 2. Ibn al-Dimyāṭī: 3. Ibn al-Rav: 1. Ibn Kawjakh: 5. Ibn Shaʿya: 5. Ibn al-Qirqisānī: 12. This is followed by the number 51.5 (or 11.5?). Dating: probably 12th century.

Bifolio of accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. The hand may be known. Dating: 11th century. Headed (recto left page): "I consulted God and purchased [...] from Dār Ibn Marwān: . . ."; goes on to mention Nahray; Ibn al-Tinnīsī; pepper; something red; thread.
Recto: Letter fragment. Very narrow. Handwriting of Avraham Maimonides? Verso: memorial list of the family of Sheʾerit b. Yefet. (Information in part from CUDL and Goitein's index card.)
Fragment of a poem praising the Nagid, whose name is only hinted at. (Information from Goitein's index cards)
Document in Arabic, probably, from which four lines of text remain. Medieval-era. Requires further examination.
Jottings of blessings in Hebrew, possibly drafts for a letter.
Late Hebrew letter in a cursive hand. On verso a drawing and few words
Accounts, mentioning names such as ha-Levi, [Abū l-]Maʿānī, Abū l-ʿAlā. (Information from CUDL)
Small letter fragment in Arabic. Excerpts: معهم واخرج جملة . . . ها الف و . . . . بذلك حتى كانه حاصل . . . Requires further examination.

State document, in Arabic script. Four fragmentary lines preserved. Dated 446 H/1054 CE. Probably a decree ordering the safeguarding of the affairs of the people under the addressee's administration. On verso, there is Hebrew poetry.
Epistle of R. Sherira Gaon. see PGPID 23194
Small fragment of a state document mentioning the amīr Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥusayn b. ʿUmar.

Legal document. Record of release. Dated 1085. Location: Alexandria. This document is a largely-complete release signed and executed by well-known members of the rabbinical court of Alexandria. The litigants are Yosef b. Shemuel and the judge Menashshe b. Pinḥas. Although the details of the relationship between the litigants are not explicitly stated, the release clauses suggest that a partnership existed between the two of them. Items listed include currency, raw and smithed precious metals, clothing, textiles, and other merchandise, suggesting that the partners were involved in a trading par
Verso: Unidentified Arabic script, may be documentary.

Fragment from the top of a letter. The opening consists of Hebrew blessings. Continues in the margin in Judaeo-Arabic: וקלבי קוי בדלך בך ו . . . ובאללה תבארך ותעאלי אול . . . . ואנא . . . מן גהתה חתי יגי אלי אן שא אללה ואנא ואתק באללה ובך ואללה יבארך פיכם . . . .

Reused for jottings and pen exercises in Hebrew and Arabic script on verso. (Information in part from FGP.)

Verso: Two distinct text blocks in Arabic script. The upper one is a record about the height of the Nile flood. Part of which reads as " اوفي النيل بفضل رب العالمين يوم الخميس سبعة في الول سبعة عشر ذراعا الحمد لله رب العالمين وصلى الله على عباده الذين اصطفى". The lower one, at 90 degrees, mostly in the same hand mentions a qāḍī. "لمولاي القاضي" meaning that the report about the Nile flood could be for the Qāḍī, and then mentions that the sender is at the disposal of the Qāḍī whenever he wants "مطالبة في اي وقت شا ان شا الله" . The report is dated according to the Jewish calendar, Thursday 7th
Communal letter in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi. Wide line spacing. ~8 lines are preserved. Reused on recto for Hebrew piyyuṭ in a different hand.

Legal and communal documents.

(a) Power of attorney granted by Saʿadya b. Yeshuʿa to Yosef b. Elʿazar ha-Melammed for the purpose of suing Yaʿaqov b. Natan Ibn Miṣbāḥ for a sum of 21.5 dinars. No signatures. Dated: last third of Sivan 1461 Seleucid = June 1150 CE.

(b) Written in a different hand. Note of a legal acknowledgment made by Bū l-Mufaḍḍal concerning receipt of funds from the wine that his father left behind, including the figure 1,937 (jars) as well as 48 dinars from the estate and 19 dinars as the price of the female slave (jāriya). 

(c) Written in a third hand (same as T-S

Letter draft from Efrayim b. Shemarya to Aharon and Shelomo the sons of Ṭoviyya ha-Shelishi, mentioning condolences on the death of Ṭoviyya, a letter which had no name on it(?), the Gaʾon (l. 11), and letters to ‘the two princes’ Ḥesed al-Tustarī and someone else. Uncited in the literature. Written around an earlier text in Arabic script (jottings?). Dating: ca. 1007–1055 CE, based on the years when Efrayim b. Shemary was active. On recto there is Arabic poetry. ASE
Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. Crude hand. Mentions belts (zunnār, zanānir) several times.
Small fragment from the bottom of a legal deed. Only a few partial signatures are preserved: [...] b. Shemarya; Ṣedaqa b. Yeshuʿa; Avraham b. Natan Av.

The main text is in Ladino and Hebrew, perhaps a sermon or exegetical work. Verso also contains: the draft of the beginning of a Ladino family letter with several drafts of the signature of Eliezer Ḥazaq; a musar text in Hebrew in a different hand; calligraphic pen trials of the Arabic alphabet; and scattered jottings and sums in Hebrew characters.

Letter from Abū Isḥāq b. Ṭayyib (same as in ENA NS 77.397 (PGPID 13697)?) to Abū [...]. Interestingly begins with the verse/motto הנה אל ישועתי. Dating: probably 13th century or later. (Information in part from CUDL)

Recto: (draft of a?) letter with jottings. The sender mentions "his headache" and the sender's intention to travel east (אלממלוך קד עזם קולא ואחדא עלי אלתוגה נחו אלשרק). Dating: probably ca. late 12th or early 13th century.

Verso: jottings. (Information from CUDL)

List of accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: Medieval era. Mentions quantities of gold dinar throughout the entries, with some crossed out. In a rudimentary hand previously misattributed to ʿArūs b. Yosef.
Fragment of a letter mentioning the elder Manṣūr. Dating: Probably 13th or 14th century, based on hand and typical abbreviations (mam[lūk], makh[dūm], sh[aykh]). (Information in part from CUDL)

Likely fiscal accounts, in very small writing. E.g. "min māl. . . al-aʿmāl..." and "wuṣūl... dīnārayn..." Underneath there may be a date (560 AH?). It seems this was used as part of a binding of a booklet of Hebrew piyyuṭim, likely by the same scribe who reused T-S NS 110.157 (PGPID 41745).

Legal record (#31) in a court register/pinqas from a beit din in Cairo (on f. 4v of T-S K22.27). In Hebrew. Location: Cairo. Dated at the end of (29) Tammuz 5458 CE, which is 1698 CE. 

(Document #31) Brief testimony by a certain Aharon Lobregón that he is leaving his daughter and "his maidservant" (שפחתו, an enslaved woman) in the home of Yosef Abzaradel while he travels to Alexandria. The entry does not state for how long Aharon planned to travel. The Sephardi surname Lobregón may be a toponym related to the small town of Obregón in northern Spain. MCD.
Business accounts in Arabic script and a few Greek/Coptic numerals. Listing various textiles/garments and prices in dirhams. Also mentions the ruqʿa of the banker (al-ṣayrafī).

Recto: legal document in Hebrew, Aramaic and Judaeo-Arabic, dated 14[.. Sel.] (= ~12th century CE), mentioning Fusṭāṭ; Moshe; al-Kātib; an oath; and a sum of dinars. Handwriting of Mevorakh b. Natan? Verso: unidentified text in Hebrew. (Information in part from CUDL)

List of names. Most entries have little circles over them. E.g., Menaḥem, [Yo]sef, Eliyya, ʿaskarī (a soldier?), al-Fakhr, Khalaf, Kāfūr (means camphor, but can be a name), al-Muhadhdhab Sulay[mān]. AA. ASE.

Legal deed. In Hebrew, with some Babylonian vocalization. Location: Fustat. Dated: Kislev 4787 AM = November/December 1026 CE. Maymūn b. Efrayim receives a loan of a sum of Muʿizzī dinars from Yosef (perhaps Ibn ʿAwkal). (Information from Goitein's index card.)

Letter from David al-Qalʿī, perhaps in Minyat Zifta or nearby, to Yosef al-Faranji (it seems his uncle), perhaps in Fustat/Cairo. In Hebrew. Dating: mid-16th century, based on Avraham David's assessment and identification of the people named. The letter deals mainly with a request for the addressee to send wheat to the writer, and gives details about how the wheat market is faring in his location. Information in part from Avraham David's edition (FGP).
Receipt for the capitation tax of Ibrāhīm b. Yūsuf, a Jewish goldsmith (yahūdī ṣāʾigh), in Fustat, for the year 537. See also T-S Ar.35.197.
Minute fragment containing legal notes. In the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe? Mentioning Yiṣḥāq b. Moshe and 27 dinars.

Small fragment from the beginning of a legal deed. In the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe (1100–38 CE). Involves Abū l-Faraj Hibatallāh and Abū Saʿd known as Ibn al-S[...]. T-S AS 220.80 (PGPID 22931) and T-S AS 220.110 (PGPID 22921) are likely related and/or an indirect join.
Minute fragment of a legal document, probably from a marriage contract. Mentions two gold dinars.
Accounts for the week of Bamidbar. Listing various names with numbers underneath.
Document in Arabic script. Narrow vertical strip.
Business-family letter showing the concern of the Jews of Egypt for those of Yemen. Dated Thursday, middle of the month Elul. (Information from Goitein's index cards)
Court record in the hand of Halfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi (fl. 1100–38 CE). Refers to a sick person whose will is invalid (...מרצה בטלת וציתה...) and a woman named Ḥusn bt. [...].
Account in Judaeo-Arabic. Mentions Abū ʿAbd Allāh; Abū Manṣūr; brass; Ghālib; Ibn al-Anṣārī.
Legal testimony. involving Sitt al-Nasab known as [...] and Abū ʿImrān known as Ibn Shumayʿ (?). The ends of the lines are missing, and the scribe abandoned the document in line 6.
Legal document in Arabic script. May be a deed of sale (hādhā mā ishtarā....). One of the parties is Jewish. Reused in the upper margins and on verso for biblical verses in Hebrew.
Letter to Abraham ‘the Great Rav’ (presumably Abraham Maimonides). (Information from CUDL)
Mostly empty except for the name b. Sai'd
Legal query with responsum. Awaiting fuller description.
Interesting poem in Judaeo-Arabic about lost beauty and youth, apparently of a woman (referred to as Sitt al-Maʿālī in l. 14).

tags: communal, illness: syrup, illness: poverty, Appeal, Sunbat, Petition, illness letter 969-1517, Illness
desc: Letter from Ibrāhīm, in Sunbāṭ, addressed to a Nagid. In Judaeo-Arabic. Requesting assistance for his family in time of need. His family members are all sick, and he has no money even for a medicinal syrup.

Letter fragment to [...] b. Ḥayyīm. In this note, the writer states that he had previously sent with the letter-bearer two books, one containing Talmud Rosh ha-Shana and Taanit and the second, a work by Hayya Gaon to be sold. (Information from Goitein's index cards)
Literary text, in Judaeo-Arabic. Discusses the Hebrew language and the language of the Bible. Could be theology or Bible exegesis. Needs examination.

Business accounts in Arabic script and Greek/Coptic numerals. One entry refers to the revenue from the shop; customs (maks); brokerage (samsara): and 83 dirhams. The next refers to Abū l-Faraj, the revenue from the shop; 140 pounds; and a guarantee or tax farming obligation (ḍamān). The next refers to Sayyid al-Ahl, 120 pounds, and the ḍamān, maks, and samsara again: qabaḍū al-ḍamān al-mutaqddimīn maksuhu wa l-samsara. Probably refers to tax in kind with units in raṭl.

Letter from Nissim b. Ḥalfon, from Tinnis, to Nahray b. Nissim, Fustat. Ca. 1055 (Gil). Regarding a shipment of textiles that Nissim b. Ḥalfon had sent to Nahray, including two expensive textiles for a Muslim customer, Abū ʿImrān Mūsā b. Ḥakam. There are three shipments mentioned in the letter. The first (r4–8) contains two garments sent via a Rūmī sailor: a fine dabīqi" garment with a single ṭirāz border and a second garment for Abū l-Faraj Ṣemaḥ, valued at 3 dinars and 2 qirats provided that it is acceptable. The second (r8–15) contains two garments, sent via Muḥsin b. Ukht al-Bantīt: a dabq
Literary text in Ladino.

A leaf from a court notebook. 

Recto: dated 1 Elul 1409 Seleucid = 1 August 1098 CE. For Ḥalfon b. Yeshuʿa known as Ibn al-Ṭārima(?), who wanted to reverse his purchase of half a house from his brother Elʿazar for the amount of 10 dinars. The financial arrangements take into account his brother's upcoming travel to al-Shām (Palestine or Damascus). Also mentions travel to upper Egypt (al-Ṣaʿīd). Not complete.

Commercial letter in Arabic script. Long and damaged. Dating: likely 16th century, as it mentions the ashrafī (used from 1425 onward but replaced by other currencies in the 16th century) and an amīr who is "very afraid of the pasha" (الباشاه), dating the document to after the Ottoman conquest in 1517. Dealing at length with merchants traveling to and from India and commodities such as pepper and ginger and camphor. Also mentions somebody who has gone up to Cairo. Needs further examination. ASE
Tax receipt? For [...] al-Yahūdī. Sum: 1/6 dinar. Needs examination.

Family letter probably addressed to a woman ("... wa-lā tajlisī..."). The sender apparently wouldn't have traveled if (s)he had known something (...fa-mā kuntu sāfartu wa-lā kharajtu aṣlan...). Mentions combs (amshāṭ). On verso, refers to plans to travel again (...an akhruja...). Asks after the children (khabar al-ṣighār). Mentions sending various things, and 8 dirhams.
Medical prescription with the order of what to do after the medicine has worked: sweet rose water, cold water, and a boiled chicken. (information from Goitein's index card). VMR

Informal note in Arabic script. (Addressed to a dignitary according to the Baker/Polliack catalog, but this does not seem to be founded.) "By God, man, I heard..." (billāh yā sīdī balaghanī...). The margins and the remaining three pages of the bifolio are filled with Judaeo-Arabic poetry.

Letter from Benaya b. Mūsā to Abū Yiṣḥaq Abraham b. Sulaymān concerning the textile business, particularly an order for a Tustari robe or cloth (al-thawb al-Dasturi) and 'large cut pieces'. The qāḍī Abū al-Faraj, Abū Naṣr b. Shaʿīd (?), Abū al-Surur, Abū al-Maʿalī, and Abū Saʿd are mentioned, along with the town of Bilbays. EMS With Coptic numerals on verso. (Information from CUDL)

Letter in Ladino from Ḥayyim Reʾuven Miris or Mires, addressed to Avraham Krispin (Crespin) in "Miṣrayim" (Cairo). Dated: 1787 CE (13 Iyyar [5]547). The author mentions receiving a letter from Avraham Crespin via Rhodes and that he also received correspondence from Shmuel Ḥanan via Izmir. The most likely location that Miris is writing from, however, seems to be Rosetta given that he recounts the recent arrival of Ib[rahim] al-Tūnsī אאון in the port city (perhaps = surname Aoun). He also recounts acquiring or perhaps visiting the homes of two widows in Rosetta: "the home of the widow of Magoro
Right side of an informal note probably addressed to R. Aharon, informing him to do something to do with 'our colleagues' without delay.
Possibly the poetic opening of a letter. But may also be literary.

tags: Yemen, Sicily, hinge, India Book unedited, ib-addenda
desc:
Recto: Opening lines of a letter introduced by quotations such as Psalms 31:2. Verso: unusual note that does not seem to be a classic address; it is written vertically and 90 degrees to the direction of the text on the other side, which suggests it was written after the fragment was already torn. It reads, "Letters from [my? your?] brother from Yemen, to be sent to Sicily/Palermo along with my letter, God willing." Maybe the letter on recto was torn to create scrap paper, and this note was then enclosed along with a bundle of letters to be forwarded from Yemen to Sicily via Egypt.

Possibly
Letter from Shelomo b. Yehuda to Avraham Ha-Kohen, Sar Ha-Eda b. Yiṣḥaq. Dating: ca. 1025–1051 CE based on the years when Shelomo b. Yehuda served as Gaʾon.
Ketubba fragment. The groom's name is Nissim. The payments amount to 100+ dinars.
Recto: Fragment of a legal document, referring to transactions and mentioning Ibn al-Bayrūtī and ‘in the hand of Abū ʿAlī ha-Levi’. Verso: jottings. (Information from CUDL)

Fragment of a report concerning members of an official’s service and resulting damage. The writer states that information had reached him concerning the followers of the addressee’s exalted service (اتباع خدمته السامية). The damaged passage mentions horses (خيولا) and mounts (niʿāl; lit. hooves), though the precise context is unclear. The writer then reports that someone remained there for an additional day and mentions extensive damage. The fragment closes with mention of his opinion regarding proceeding/advancing toward something or somewhere (ورأيه في التقدم إلى [...]), but the destination

Literary narrative in Arabic script. 1001 nights? Mentions a baker and a salesman, then the narrator stumbles on a hidden treasure with a magical sapphire, then winds up at the king's palace. T-S NS 306.167 is probably another small piece of this book.

Recto: Note from a certain ʿUzziel. In Judaeo-Arabic. Explaining that the collection of pledges (pesiqa) has been delayed because it was mismanaged from the outset. The sender says he is always trying to expedite it, and he will deal with the matter as soon as he is free. Dating: ca. 12th–13th century. (S. D. Goitein, Mediterranean Society 2:544) EMS. Verso: Business accounting in Judaeo-Arabic and in Arabic script. (Information from CUDL)
Original use: Fiscal account in Arabic script, mentioning wheat and various districts and an ʿāmil. Needs examination.

Bifolio of accounting for the purchase of wax (sharḥ shary al-shamʿ). Mentions Nuʿmān; pepper; the word אכדת is spelled אכת; selling a turban to Salāma; the term tashmīʿ (presumably somethign to do with wax); the customs at Dār Mānak and other payments. The right page of recto is headed "explanation of the indigo which I left [in] Almeria with Abū ʿUmar b. BQNṢ(?)

Verso: Accounts in Arabic and Greek/Coptic numerals. Detailing sums collected from various people (Maḥfūḍ, Bū l-ʿIzz al-Sharābī, Hilāl, Makkī(?)). Also detailing what is owed by Bū l-Faraj and others. 

Recto: There is a list of Coptic numerals of unclear significance. At 90 degrees, there are two lines in Judaeo-Arabic: "I took an oath not to break my fast on Sunday in the town. And peace." (חלפת מא אפטר יום אלאחד פי אלבלד ושלום)

Letter from Ismail b. Yitzhak ha-Andalusi, Jerusalem, to Nahray b. Nissim, Fustat. Around 1065. Blessings for the holiday. The writer asks to pass an attached letter to his mother and brother in Spain. (Information from Gil, Palestine, vol. 3, pp. 285-287, #512) VMR

A letter explaining what happened in the synagogue t the writer and Munajjā b. Ṭāhir and Barakāt Ibn al-ʿAṭṭār. He also sends regards to David ha-Nagid (unclear if David I or David II). Other names mentioned: [...] b. Bashāsh and Bunayn. AA

Densely written mercantile accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. Very difficult to read.

Same hand:
T-S NS 69.4 (PGPID 26151)
T-S NS 223.74 (PGPID 23973)
T-S AS 158.155 (PGPID 41643)

End of a legal document, signed by David b. Mevorakh, Abraham b. Caleb and others. Below is a colophon written by Elʿazar b. Joseph b. ʿAmram, also mentioning Yefet b. Ṭoviyya. (Information from CUDL)

Bill of divorce, fragment. Husband: Maʿānī b. Khalaf. Wife: Jamīʿ bt. Barakāt (both families are from Minyat Ziftā, Egypt). Dated: Friday, 29 Sivan 1426 Seleucid, which is 1115 CE. Location and names of any witnesses are not preserved. See also nearby fragments T-S 10J3 ff. 2-11, fragments of bills of divorce. (Information from CUDL and Goitein’s index card)

tags: Qaraite, illness letter 969-1517, illness: recovered, illness: public figure, Illness, 12th c
desc: Recto: Letter from a Karaite in Alexandria to the Karaite Nasi David b. Hasdai, concerning support for the Nasi from the Karaite communities in the Maghreb. Dating: 12th century. The letter opens with many very deferent phrases and congratulations on the addressee's recovery from illness. Verso: Draft of a rhymed Hebrew opening to a letter. (Information from CUDL)

Jottings in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi (fl. 1100–1138 CE). The top line names a dead person and 'his sister Fākhira.' The next lines give weights of various substances such as boxthorn (khawlān), opium (afyūn), and something black.
Jottings of business accounts

Two different legal documents. One of them is catalogued as a deed of sale. These are folios 2 and 3; folio 1 is literary. The document on fol. 2 involves a deceased man [...]b and his deceased brother ʿImrān. Handwriting of Hillel b. ʿEli? (Information in part from FGP.)

Booklist in Judaeo-Arabic listing individual Epistles of the Brethren of Purity. Booklist. E.g., "Third: Epistle elucidating the beliefs of the Brethren of Purity and the sects of the holy divines (madhāhib al-rabbāniyyīn al-ilāhiyyīn; this probably does not refer to Rabbanites). Fourth: Epistle on the methods of the community of the Brethren of Purity and Friends [of Loyalty]...." It continues with "[Fifth]" and "Sixth" on verso. ASE
Deed of sale for a female slave. The seller is probably al-Ḥusna or al-Ḥasana bt. Yoshiyya and the buyer is either Mevorakh or [...] b. Mevorakh. (Information in part from CUDL)
Address of a letter in Hebrew to Meʾir the cantor, with, beneath it, (the same?) address in Arabic (to the elder Abū l-[...]). (Information from CUDL)

Letter fragment from an unknown writer to his son (probably). Written in Judaeo-Arabic. The introduction is preserved, wherein the writer says he is proud of hearing about the son upholds his honor (qayyim al-jāh), and the concluding greetings are preserved, including to R. Seʿadya and R. Eliyya.
Guide to the numerical value of the Arabic letters.

Damaged legal deed, probably a settlement, in which a man (Manṣ[ūr]?) accepts a number of stipulations upon himself concerning a house and household goods. He agrees not to annoy (ḍājara) his wife, and he will provide for the two daughters of Yaʿqūb b. M[...] Ibn Jumayʿ, who are named Sitt al-Ahl and Sitt al-Qawām. The situation is not totally clear; this might be a divorce agreement or another kind of agreement based on the conditions that were written in the ketubba. At the bottom of verso, at 180 degrees, there is an unrelated legal note concerning the marriage payments of Elʿazar b. Ṭ[...]

Fragment from the bottom of a ketubba. Groom: Ṣemaḥ ha-Levi ha-Parnas. The bride's name is missing; this is not her first marriage. Part of the dowry list is preserved. The witnesses include Ḥalfon b. Saʿadya and Elʿazar b. Menaḥem, both of whom have crude handwriting.

Letter to a sister named Sitt Suʿūd, in Fustat. The scribe is Elʿazar b. Ahuv and the address states that the letter should be delivered to Yefet b. Shemuʾel. Conveying congratulations, it seems on the birth of a daughter to the addressee. Others send their congratulations, including Umm Abū l-Faḍl, Abū l-Majd, Abū Manṣūr, Abū l-Fakhr, and Umm Hiba. Mentions a messenger Abū l-Faraj b. אלוש(?). Mentions having paid the price of the blanket (l. 27). Might be related to L-G Misc. 68 (PGPID 35021), which mentions a blanket for Sitt Suʿūd (an uncommon name). (Information in part from Goitein's inde

Recto: Legal query in the hand of Moshe b. Levi ha-Levi addressed to Maimonides, who was active in Egypt ca. 1168–1204 CE. Concerning partners in a business venture; the traveling partner returned with safflower (ʿuṣfur) but there was no market for it, so it was kept for a time until there should be a market for it. During this period, the traveling partner died without a will in the Jewish courts, leaving minor children. The case is quite convoluted and there follow more details.

Letter/petition to a certain David ha-Sar in which the writer asks him to intercede on his behalf with al-Sadīd. Dating: late 12th or early 13th century. The sender's name originally appeared in the right margin.

Bifolio of accounts in Judaeo-Arabic and Arabic and Greek/Coptic numerals. Dating: probably 12th or 13th century. Organized by parshiyot. Mentions Barakāt al-Qazzāz b. Sulaymān; Sukkot (ʿīd al-miẓalla); mulūkhiyya; olive oil; linseed oil; pigeons; green lemons; possibly palm fronds for the sukka (jarīd li-l-miẓalla); chickens. The facing page on verso is headed "account of my lord [...]"; mentions Yūsuf al-Ṭabbākh.

Letter from Moshe b. Shemuel b. Jami, probably sent from Fustat to his partner in Qabes, mentioning merchandise in the Maghreb and Egypt, and asking Hayya Gaon to find him a good copy of one of the parts of the Mishnah that he could not find in Fustat. (Information from Gil)
One or two words in cursive Latin script: P Nicolas(?).
Commercial accounts that seem to be in Portuguese (vinegar, pepper, and other commidities). Identified by Eleazar Gutwirth.
Accounts in Arabic script and Greek/Coptic numerals. Dating: late, looks Ottoman-era.
Deed of sale of a property. Many landmarks and characteristics are described.

Business or official letter in Arabic script, top only; continues on verso. Likely from Ḥamīd b. Qāsim to a qāḍī; mentions Abū l-Ḥasan b. Salīm. Reused for a Judaeo-Arabic text on recto and verso, according to Baker and Polliack about Alexander the Great; mentions China (al-Ṣīn) several times.

tags: illness: consilia, toilet, illness: gastrointestinal, Illness: physician, Illness, illness letter 969-1517, Illness: treatment, illness: prescription, illness: cost
desc: Recto and beginning of verso: Letter from a sick man to a physician. In Judaeo-Arabic. He reports that he has collected the prescription that the physician gave him and that he used it earlier in the day, but it had no effect. He is still in great and unmentionable distress whenever he leaves the toilet (murtafaq). He has sent the (substantial amount of) 109.5 dirhams that the physician charged him. He asks for further instructions, because he is in great distress. He is unable to leave the house but cannot bear sitting in in the house. Lower part of verso: The physician responds that the medi
Letter fragment in Judaeo-Arabic. Mentions lāsīn silk and Fustat and someone who has spent 2 years somewhere. Hand of Yefet b. Menashshe?

Unidentified, with biblical citations such as Psalms 137:6 and 41:6. List of piyyuṭim? On verso there are also formulae typical of a petition. Dating: probably ca. 13th century. (Information in part from CUDL)
Accounts in the hand of ʿArūs b. Yosef.
Verso: Jotted account in Arabic script and Greek/Coptic numerals. Mentions a bible (muṣḥaf) with the number 2 (𐋢) underneath. May be related to recto.
State document, in Arabic script. Fragment from the beginning of a petition. Dating: likely Ayyubid or Mamluk.

tags: Illness, illness: du'f, illness: prayer, illness: ghurba, illness letter 969-1517, distant husband, Hebron
desc: Letter from an unknown writer, probably in Hebron, to his wife (addressed as al-Sitt al-Jalīla), probably in Fustat. Addressed to al-Shaykh al-Muhadhdhab al-Khayyāṭ (the tailor), possibly the wife's father. In Judaeo-Arabic. The writer reports that he developed a serious illness (ḍuʿf ṣaʿb) in Hebron. He is sustained only by her prayers and his knowledge of her righteousness. He departed on this journey because business had ground to a halt and he needed to gain a living. (Information in part from Goitein’s note cards.) EMS. ASE.

tags: Nahray B. Nissim, commodities, silk, trade
desc:
Letter from Mardūkh b. Mūsā in Alexandria to Nahray b. Nissim in Fustat. (c. July 1048 CE). Mardūkh expresses outrage as he reports on the opening of a bundle of commodities passing through Alexandria on its way to Fustat; the goods included a qintar and forty jarwī raṭls of wax and a bundle of silk (khazz). The letter also mentions an order for what Goitein interprets as earthenware goblets ("sājira") with gold luster. (S. D. Goitein, Mediterranean Society, 1:337, 487; 4:149, 394; Jessica Goldberg, Trade and Institutions in the Medieval Mediterranean, 173.) EMS 

Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm Ibn al-Is
Letter fragment. Beginning in rhymed Hebrew and continuing in Judaeo-Arabic. Spanish-influenced hand. Requests a "cheering" (letter) and conveys blessings to the addressee. AA/ASE
Accounts. Written on the back of an earlier fiscal document (see separate entry).
Letter, probably. Tiny fragment, containing only the first ~3 words and last ~3 words. From "Yedid b. Yosef ha-Levi."
An urgent summons to appear before the court from the office of Yehoshua Maimonides (b. 1310–d. 1355 CE).

Huge model of a begging letter. In Hebrew and Judaeo-Arabic. From one who boasts to have belonged to ‘the owners of money’ (aṣḥāb al-amwāl) and became one of those who lost their riches (מיורדים מנכסיהם). Written on a bifolium. One of the pages has Ezekiel 1, another has love poetry in Judaeo-Arabic. (Information in part from Goitein’s index card.)

Minute fragment from the end of a letter or legal document, probably in the hand of Avraham Maimonides. Ends ve-shalom. Only a few words are legible. T-S AS 169.122 and T-S AS 169.124 may belong together.

Document in Arabic script. Accounts of some kind, or probably fiscal. Undeciphered and needs examination. In the margins and on verso there is Hebrew literary text, probably poetry. The word עין is repeated several times.

Letter from Yeshua ha-Kohen b. Yosef in Alexandria to the community of Fustat. The handwriting is Yeshua's and the letter is written in rhymed prose. (Information from Frenkel. See additional information in Goitein, Med. Soc. 5:367-8 and Bareket, Shafrir Miṣrayim, 18 (notice there is a mistake in Frenkel's 'mentioned' list: Goitein deals with this letter in volume 5 of Med. Soc. and not in volume 4. The page in volume 5 is 368 and not 68. She also does not mention Bareket's edition). While Bareket claims that the letter was sent from Jerusalem, Goitein claims that it was sent from Alexandria.
Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic on recto and verso, some are crossed out. Medieval-era. Requires further examination.
Accounts. Mentions rose water.
Minute fragment- few words in Arabic - needs examination.

Legal document dated ‘middle [decade] of Av’ [...], most likely from Fusṭāṭ, mentioning [...] the perfumer (al-ʿaṭṭār) al-Levi; Abū [...] Peqid ha-Soḥarim Kelil ha-Yofi b. [...] (this is probably Meshullam b. Elʿazar ha-Kohen based on the titles); and Abū l-ʿAlāʾ. Also refers to a transfer of a sum of money and an agreement (ittifāq). (Information in part from CUDL)
Mirrored script only. Probably an account in the hand of Abū Zikrī Kohen. Mentions Ramaḍān.
Decree, probably. "... wa-amr amīr al-muʾminīn..." Reused between the lines for an Arabic-script text, apparently a Jewish exegetical work since there are Hebrew words interspersed.
Literary text, in Arabic script. Two sides, probably an extract from a larger text. The text personifies different minerals and botany, where each debates with the other about who is superior.

Unusual document containing meeting minutes relating to the business dealings of someone whose name is too faded to read (r2). In Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: probably 13th or 14th century. The handwriting is distinctive and may be known. 
 
(1) Mentions Muḥammad, al-Rav, and collecting and numbering and registering "copies." 
(2) Meeting with Zekharya ha-Sofer: regarding copies and blank notebooks and exhorting him to fulfill prior instructions ("and let there be no third party other than God") and to bind the book that had been left with him. 
(3) Meeting with Dāʾūd al-Maghribī: informing him

Legal document in Arabic script. Dating: Mentions "497" which is likely referring to a hijrī year, in which case this would date to ca. 1103/04 CE. The document mentions a mosque (al-masjid) numerous times. It seems to be about the mosque rather than simply citing it as as landmark, since it also refers to the mosque's administrator (mutawallī al-masjid al-madhkūr). Needs further examination.

Court record(s). In the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi (active 1100–38). On recto, the court certifies the receipt of something which was due to Sitt al-Ḥusn bt. Abū Manṣūr Sahl/Shela ha-Kohen probably from Abū l-Faraj Shemuel ha-Zaqen Rosh ha-Qehillot (appears also in Moss. V,393.1 (PGPID 18093)). The continuation is missing. Verso is difficult to read and may or may not be related.
Memorial lists, mentioning Netanʾel ha-Levi and [Abū] l-Ḥasan Ibn al-Fāḍil b. [...]. Mainly in Hebrew, with some Arabic (in Arabic script) interspersed. (Information mainly from CUDL)

Recto (secondary use): court record in the hand of Natan b. Shemuel. Dating: ca. 1145 CE or, more broadly, ca. 1128–1164 CE based on the years when Natan b. Shemuʾel he-Ḥaver was active. Dealing with the case of an oil merchant who had borrowed 20 dinars from a Muslim four years before and had not repaid it. A clothier, who had stood bail for the oil merchant, was given permission by the court to sell two gold bracelets deposited with him by the oil merchant. (Information from CUDL)

tags: kurush, 18th or 19th c, ledger, numismatic dating
desc: List of accounts on a bifolium that may have once comprised a broader financial ledger. The method of bookkeeping is terse but relies on a predictable structure in which each entry is designated on a daily basis. On the verso, two forms of Ottoman coinage are referenced along the right margin of the fragment: "sherifi" and "kurush", which are accompanied by notes in both Hebrew alphanumerical figures and eastern Arabic numerals. The presence of silver kuruş is useful in estimating the dating of the document as 18th or 19th-century– given that these coins were minted as early as 1690 but did no

tags: 11th c, Yisrael b. Natan, trade, Tyre, Nahray B. Nissim
desc: Letter from Yisrael b. Natan, Tyre, to Nahray b. Nissim, Fustat, ca. 1060 in the month of Ab.

Continuation of a long business letter sent from Alexandria to Cairo. Dating: Ca. 1235 CE, based on the date of T-S Ar.54.66 which is by the same sender (and may even be the first two pages of the present letter). The scribe may be Ṭahor b. Avraham. This is either the third folio of the letter, containing pages 5 and 6, or the second folio, containing pages 3 and 4; the Greek/Coptic numeral for "3" appears at the top of recto. The sender gives the prices of merchandise in Alexandria, such as indigo, olibanum, cinnamon, brazilwood and pepper and of the taxes and other dues that have to be paid

On recto, there are morning benedictions. On verso, there are several lines of Arabic script in a calligraphic but childish hand. Seems to be copied from the title verso of a manuscript attributed to Ibn Sina. Needs examination.

Fragment of a letter. 6 lines in Hebrew with praises for an important person (including that God make his enemies drink poison), then 1 line in Judaeo-Arabic beginning a letter of recommendation for the bearer: . . . סבב אצדאר הדה אלכדמה אלי מולאי אלשיך החכם] והנבון הירא שמים יהי אלהיו עז[רו] ואויביו ישקה כוס רעל ויכלה בטוב ימיו ובנעימים שנותיו יחיה לו חמודו . . . השר הנכבד התלמיד המיבין יזכהו לראות בניו ובני בניו ממלאים מקום אבותם הטהורים הקדושים וכן יהי רצון אעלאמה דאם עזה באן חאמלה[א] . . . .

Fiscal document with multiple sections; conjoined tax receipts that have either been glued together or not yet cut apart. The lower fragment has registrations above it e.g. "yuthbat bi-dīwān al-ishrāf." Payment of 34 dinars? Needs further examination.

Verso is a table of Greek/Coptic numerals, which may or may not be related.

Letter from Shemuel b. Ḥofni to Shemarya b. Maṣliaḥ, probably the father of Efrayim b. Shemarya, the leader of the Palestinian Jewish community in Fustat in the first half of the 11th century. Only part of the introduction on recto and the address on verso have been preserved. (Information from Gil, Kingdom, Vol. 2, p. 156.)

tags: suftaja, Nahray B. Nissim, 11th c, private, account
desc: Private accounts of Abu Zikri Tabib in the hand of Nahray b. Nissim (Goitein) or Yehuda b. Saadya (Gil). Dating: ca. 1065 (Gil). Draft. Mentions the money that Yehuda b. Sa’adya owed and paid. Yehuda was the Nagid of the Jews in Egypt. He was a doctor but was also involved in the trading business, especially of pearls. Bifolio written on three pages, all crossed out. (Information from Gil, Kingdom, vol. 2, p. 901, and Goitein's index cards)

Letter fragment. In Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: Ca. 1107 CE, since Ṣāʿid al-Dimashqī appears also in T-S 13J2.15 from that year. The sender of this letter gives a report about "the stone" (al-ḥajar). He went to Ṣāʿid al-Dimashqī and asked him [...]. Then he went to see Ḥusayn b. Rosh ha-Qahal, who was with a customer of his, and [...]. The sender told Ḥusayn that the stone belonged to Rabbenu [...]. Then they weighed it "without nafaḍ" and it came out to [...] (. . . ואכרגת אלחגר [פ]מא סוי פי אלסוק סתה ונצף וד[. . .] . . . אלא אן מצית אלי ענד צאעד אלדמשקי וסאלתה פי . . . פמצית קלת לחסין בן ראש הקהל
Legal queries and/or responsa.

Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. Revenue from rent. Dated: Dhū l-Qaʿda [644 AH] = Nisan 1558 Seleucid, which is March/April 1247 CE. Small fragment, recording payments for one month, and containing the names of 13 tenants. (Information in part from Gil, Documents, doc. #141, pp.470f.)
Legal document, small fragment. Involves [...] b. Yūsuf and a certain Faraj. Signed by Yefet b. Yesh[aʿya?]

Letter in Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: Perhaps 12th century. Wide space between the lines, like an official document, but it appears to be about business. Mentions Ibn Zakkār. The sender orders several miʿjars, at least one with embroidery (ṭirāz). Also orders dabīqī cloth. Also mentions something about 'placing the risk on its owner / his friend' (4 lines from the bottom).
Accounts, probably. In Arabic script and possibly Greek/Coptic numerals. On verso there is liturgical text in Hebrew. (Information in part from CUDL)

Bottom of a legal document in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe. Dated: First decade of Iyyar 1438 Seleucid, which is 1127 CE. Little of the content is preserved. Mentions "one third" and possibly the name Musallam. (Information in part from CUDL)

Legal document concerning a quittance of debt, dated 1446 Sel. (1135 CE). Signed by Ḥalfon b. Menashshe and Elʿazar b. Yosef. Mentions Yaʿqūb Abū l-Maʿālī b. Yūsuf, known as Ibn Kujik (כוגך, Kushek, Persian 'Small') and Abū ʿAlī b. Shemuʾel b. Shelomo, known as Ibn al-Dustarī. Bifolio 2r of a court register in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe consisting of four pages and containing four court cases.
(Information in part from CUDL)
Minute fragment from an opening of a legal deed. AA
Ketubba with a valuable dowry listing gold jewellery, pearls, rubies, and turquoise, second half of the 15th century. (Corrected by comparison with photocopy of MS & Goitein's notes) (Z.F.)

Legal document. In Hebrew. Concerning a debt of 52 Venetian ducats (peraḥim) owed by Avraham Aripol (אריפול) to Yaʿaqov Castro (קשטרו). Dated: Monday, 20 Av 5348 AM, which is 1588 CE. Location: Fustat/Cairo. Written by Yosef b. Meʾir Somekh (סומך) ha-Kohen. At the foot of the page is a postscript in a different hand, signed Yom Ṭov Miṭrani (מטראני), confirming the document was approved by R. Beṣalel Ashkenazi (אשכנזי). (Information from CUDL)

Receipt for the capitation tax of Ibrāhīm b. Yūsuf the Jew, a silk worker (qazzāz) and craftsman (ṣāniʿ). Same payer: T-S Ar.34.224, T-S Ar.34.282 (where he is called qazzāz wa-ʿaṭṭār instead), T-S Ar.35.55, and T-S Ar.35.22. This fragment has text in 5 different hands.
Fragment of a dowry list, written on top margin of a literary text
List in Judaeo-Arabic, mentions Badr al-Dīn in the heading. 16th- or 17th-century based on the paleography.
Accounts and calculations in Arabic with Indo-Arabic numerals. Early modern. The verso has an entry "in the hand of al-Sayyid Aḥmad". Requires further examination.
Maimonides, Mishne Tora, Hilkhot Tefilla u-Nesiʾat Kappayim 14:7-15:12; Hilkhot Tefillin u-Mezuza 1:1-10 with sporadic Persian (not Arabic) supralinear glosses. (Information in part from CUDL.)
Minute fragment from a financial account. Late.

Document of a full-fledged barāʾa (release of spouse from obligations upon divorce) in which a husband (Abū l-Ḥasan b. Abū l-Faraj) and wife (Maʿālī bt. Manṣūr) from al-Maḥalla appear before the court of Fustat. Dated: Tuesday, 25 Av 4973 AM (=1524 Seleucid), which is August 1213 CE, under the reshut of Avraham Maimonides.
Possibly accounts on verso. Hebrew literary text on recto.

Letter from Menashshe b. Moshe (of Zawīlat al-Mahdiyya?) to a judge (in Fustat?). In Judaeo-arabic. Concerning a power of attorney for which 1 dinar was paid, and the belongings of Abū Saʿd b. ʿAllūn the Qaraite kātib. The sender hints that he may be forced to file a complaint with the Nagid. Possibly connected with T-S 20.187. Also mentions Salāma and Abū Baḥr(?) Yona b. Ishāq. (Information mainly from Goitein's index card.)

Letter from al-Mubārak b. Yosef b. Yazdād, Yosef b. Binyamin, and Ḥasan b. Tayyib in Fustat, to two former partners of a deceased man asking them to appear immediately in order to settle the estate of that man's orphan. These three men had been appointed the orphan's guardians by Abū Avraham Ismāʿīl b. Avraham. Related to T-S 16.27. (Information from Bareket, Shafrir misrayim)

tags: Illness: treatment, wine, illness: wine, Illness: bloodletting, illness letter 969-1517, Illness
desc: Informal note from an unknown writer to R. Ḥiyya. In Judaeo-Arabic. The writer requests the excellent jug of wine (al-nabīdh al-mamzūj) that Ḥiyya had promised him on Saturday, as he received bloodletting today, and the doctor prescribed that he drink wine afterward. Trans. Goitein, Med Soc IV, 255.
Complete letter to Abu Zikri, who is hailed as 'brother' by the writer, discussing a business dispute in a past partnership between the two. (Information from Goitein's index cards)

Recto: poetic letter in square script. Each line ends in the rhyme -let and is followed by a dot. Letters are extended to give a (mostly) neat left-hand margin. The final word of the last line is put in the middle of the page. No names preserved, but does address אדוני. Worman states that it was ‘sent by a son of Yehoshuaʿ the Ḥaver to Yehoshuaʿ’s brother’, but there is no trace of this in the fragment now. Verso: collection of halakhic rulings regarding marriage, which continues in the blank space under the letter on recto, overwriting the final word. (Information from CUDL)

Letter from Yehoshuaʿ he-Ḥaver b. Eli, Caesarea (Ḥaṣor), to the Nagid Mevorakh b. Saʿadya. Dating: ca. 1098. Apparently written after the Fatimids had reconquered Palestine. Requesting a letter from Mevorakh to the judge of Ceasarea granting Yehoshuaʿ permission to move to Ascalon, which is better fortified and safer. (Information from Gil.)

Small fragment of a state document. Very large writing, wide line spacing. Refers to someone who "severed the ambitions of the en[emies?]" ...سرم فطم مطامع الاعـ[ـدا(؟) . . . ]ملي الله عليه قيام الا . . . . Reused for Hebrew piyyuṭ, likely by the same scribe who reused T-S NS 235.62 (PGPID 41746).
Large list with entries in Hebrew. 16th-century or later based on the paleography. Requires further examination.
Fragment from a bill of divorce (get). AA

Recto: Legal document written by ʿEli b. ʿAmram. Dated: Thursday, 20 Av 1368 Seleucid, which is 1057 CE. A release for Bahiyya, wife of Mevorakh b. Efrayim, of a debt paid by her husband. Signed by Yeshuʿa b. Avraham ha-Levi, ʿEli b. Ḥayyim/Yaʿīsh ha-Kohen and Yefet b. Ṭoviyya ha-Levi. (Information in part from E. Bareket, Shafrir Misrayim, p. 271) For recto, see separate entry.

Family letter in Judaeo-Arabic informing the addressee of matters concerning Sitt Maqṣūra (NB: this is not a name but the word maqṣūdhā meaning 'her intention'), also mentioning her sister Sitt Māṭruṣa (מאטרצ֗ה) (this is also not a name but means "she is not content with X" (ما ترضى). Dating: ca. 14th–17th century. (Information in part from CUDL.) Mentions orphans several times. Needs further examination.

Verso: Receipt issued to Abū l-Ḥasan b. Wahb for his ḍamān on dyeing in Madīnat al-Fayyūm. Dated: 21 Dhū l-Qaʿda 403 (Khan reads 26 Dhū l-Qaʿda 403). Measurements: 8.7 × 8.5 cm. Written by the jahbadh Mīkhāʾīl b. ʿAbd al-Masīḥ. Amount of payment: one-half, one-third, and one-eighth dīnār and two ḥabbas (Khan reads two, one-half, one-third and one-eighth). Other texts on the same support: The recto contains part of a letter concerning ships, a commercial partnership (ṣuḥba), and a qāḍī. It was written before the verso.
Beginning of a note or letter, possibly a draft. (Information from CUDL)

Letter fragment in Judaeo-Arabic. Dated: 444, probably 444 AH = 1052/53 CE, but could theoretically be [1]444 Seleucid = 1132/33 CE. Approximately three lines on recto are preserved. The sender refers to the addressee as 'my brother' and alludes to how well he has treated him. Mentions a letter from Abū Saʿīd.

Letter fragment in Hebrew. The sender has no one to lend him even a penny; mentions every Sunday, Wednesday, and Friday being taken out to the dīwān and humiliated; the son of a certain Yosef; a request from the Nagid; and a hope that the sender will not be thrown into prison. AA/ASE

tags: Illness: women's, Byzantium, pregnancy, medical charity, physician treating family, Materia medica, Illness, illness: death, illness letter 969-1517, illness: poverty, medical books, Illness: physician, Silifke, physician, Crusades, mail-order medicine
desc: Letter from a physician in Silifke (Seleucia) to his sister's husband, presumably in Fustat. Dated 21 July 1137. "The Emperor John II Comnenus was on his way to Antioch—held at that time by Raymond of Poitiers—and a part of his powerful army passed through the town in which this letter was written. The Byzantines arrived before the gates of Antioch on August 29. Our letter, however, reports a rumor that the city had already fallen forty days earlier. The writer, a physician, even expresses the expectation that the Emperor might take Aleppo and Damascus as well and already placed an order for m

Torn court record, probably a bill of release, between Abū Yaʿqūb Yūsuf (Abū Yaʿaqov Yosef) al-Ḥarīrī and Abū l-Barakāt Yehoshuaʿ regarding a missing shipment of silk (?). The speaker was obliged to lay low due to debts owed to the dīwān. He petitioned the Nagid (שר השרים ונגיד הנגידים, probably Moshe b. Mevorakh, r. 1112–27 CE) who beneficently helped him. AA/ASE
Small fragment of an Arabic document. Damaged and faded.

Letter in the hand of Yefet b. Menashshe probably to one of his brothers. Fragment (a piece from the right side of recto). The addressee is not clearly identified. There are greetings to his brother Ḥalfon's wife Sitt Naʿīm. Also the addressee's "mother and sisters" are mentioned. Yefet reports that Ḥassūn b. ʿAllūn arrived. Mentions Baqāʾ. Mentions a radda (a garment alternately identified as "scarf" or "turban"). Mentions Cairo. (Information in part from CUDL)

Letter from Sahlān b. [...] to Abū Zakariyyā. Dating: mid-11th century. Regarding a silk binding that a Spanish person gave the addressee with instructions who should receive it. The binding belonged to Abū l-Faraj Yeshaʿya's assistant. The addressee does not give it, because he thinks that it belongs to the writer, and the writer owes him money. (Information from Gil, Kingdom, Vol. 4, #768) VMR

Verso: Legal document. Copy of a divorce settlement, dated 11th Adar I 4973 (= 1213 CE), from Alexandria, in which Yeshuʿa b. Yosef b. Raṣon Tinnīsī declares that he is bankrupt and thus unable to pay the second installment, thirty dinars, that is still outstanding from the original marriage contract, to his wife, Sitt al-Kull bt. Shelomo b. Zekharya. The debt is divided into fifteen-dirham 'of good silver' monthly payments, but if he is unable to pay this amount, he must give half of his wage day-by-day instead. Other stipulations forbid Yeshuʿa from leaving Alexandria for four years and from

State document, report, in Arabic script. Chancery hand (though not the best), with widened space between the lines, and with white space used to divide sections. The ends of 9 lines are preserved. Mentions "ghilmān li-sayyidī Asad Allāh" (l.1), "Sayyidnā al-Ustādh" (l. 3) and amīrs (ll. 4 and 9) and Abū l-Faraj (l. 8). Reused on recto for Hebrew liturgy, including biblical verses from Nehemiah 1:6–11. Needs further examination.
Legal document mentioning [...] al-Ṣayrafī b. Khalfa. Small fragment (upper right corner). Location: Fustat. (Information from CUDL)
Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic, Arabic script, and Greek/Coptic numerals. Mentions items such as jars, grapes, raw sugar (qand), water, kishk, "help for Ṭayyib," something for Isḥāq

tags: Abu l-Hasan b. Wahb, daman, tax receipt
desc: Tax receipt issued to Abū l-Ḥasan b. Wahb for his ḍamān on dyeing in Madīnat al-Fayyūm. Dated: 25 Ramaḍān 405. Amount of payment: one-half dīnār. Payment made under the supervision of three officials: (1) the auspicious, rightly guided qāḍī Thiqat al-Mulk Makīn al-Dawla wa-Amīnuhā, protégé of the Commander of the Faithful, Abū l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. Nahār; (2) (in) the presence of the fiduciary qāḍī Abū ʿAlī l-Ḥasan b. Yaḥyā b. Nahār on his behalf; (3) (under) the tax accounting of the elder Sadīd al-Dawla Abū l-Faraj ʿAbd al-Masīḥ b. Qūrīl. Measurements: 15.2 × 8.4 cm.

tags: Arus b. Yosef, Ibn Sha'ya, suftaja
desc: Letter from Sulaymān b. al-Mubārak (Shelomo b. Mevorakh) he-ḥazzan to Abū l-Afrāḥ ʿArūs b. Yūsuf. Signed by the writer. Mentions Ibn Shaʿyā.

Legal fragment mentioning Abū Manṣūr and [Abū l-]Faraj, and at least Abū Manṣūr is a kohen. Handwriting of Eliyyahu the Judge? Refers to 16 shares in a house as well as various kinds of equipment typical of druggists. (Information in part from CUDL)
Document in Arabic script. Ends of a few lines. Wide space between the lines.
Recipes in Arabic script, maybe alchemical.

List of books that [...] al-Dawla Abū l-Barakāt inherited from the late Abū l-[...]. The first two items are difficult to read (except for maqāla in both and al-malikī in item 2). The remaining items are two volumes of Kitāb al-Filāḥa, a volume of al-Mutanabbī, a volume of Adab al-Kātib, a volume of ashʿār wa-tuḥaf (sounds like a literary anthology), a volume containing a grammar treatise, and two volumes of Kitāb al-Aghānī. 10 books altogether. Dated: Tuesday, 1[8?] Av. The first two items are called نسخة and the remainder جزء. ASE

Letter of condolence (possibly a copy) to a public figure. In Hebrew and Judaeo-Arabic. Quotes Jeremiah 15:2. The name Faḍl appears in l. 1, [Abū l-Ḥa]san b. Abū Sahl (ZL) in l. 6, and Abū Yaʿaqov (perhaps the recently deceased) in l. 11. All of these are names found in the Tustarī family; needs further examination to pinpoint the specific context and dating. (Information in part from CUDL)
Unidentified document or text in Arabic script written on blue cloth. The format looks literary.
On recto piyyut. On verso fragment from a ketubbah contains mostly the dowry list. AA

Enigmatic list or glossary, in which each Arabic phrase is paired with an apparently nonsensical translation or code word. Speculation: possibly a trade argot of cheesemongers or grocers? At least five varieties of cheese are listed, including ḥālūm (the same term as modern halloumi). Some examples:
الغسيل (؟) ← الزنقال
الدكان ← الكيرونة
جبن شامي ← معدود زهراوي 
حالوم ← معدود هالم
جبن سناري ← معدود . وادي
جبن مقلي ← معدود ملرخ
الجزر ← الكفح
الجزيرة ← الكفيحة
الجزا ← الكفلي(؟)
الطبيخ ← الطوام
الدار ← القيسومة
القاعة ← البكمة

Business letter from Abū l-Surūr b. David to Abū l-Afrāḥ ʿArūs b. Yūsuf. Fragment. Mentions the late Abū Saʿīd and the Muslims who claimed they were owed money from his estate. Mentions the daughter of the late Abū l-Faraj. Verso was reused for a few lines of accounts in Judaeo-Arabic.
Letter opening, fragmentary, from Yosef ha-Kohen b. Shelomo Gaon to a friend (11th century).
Accounts in Arabic on verso with Greek/Coptic alphanumerals. Medieval-era.
One side has many lines of Judaeo-Arabic, very faded. The other side has two columns of numbers in Hebrew script, perhaps calendrical jottings or accounts.
Recto: Top of a letter in poetic Hebrew addressed to a dignitary, perhaps the Nagid: ויודע דעת עליון שר הזמן ונסיכו . . . ייי דרכו נגיד מישרם . . . .

tags: Nasi, bustanay, polemic, literary with documentary value, Exilarch
desc: Polemical composition narrating the story of the exilarch Bustanay. For a parallel text and fuller description, see PGPID 6078.
Jottings in Judaeo-Arabic and Arabic script, some of which mention al-Mawlā al-Makīn and a power of attorney (wikāla or wakāla). Dating: Perhaps late 12th or early 13th century.

Upper part of a legal document. Abū l-Bishr b. Abū l-Riḍā grants a release to ד..יה bt. Mufarrij the wife of Abū l-Ḥasan Ibn Qaṭṭūs concerning goods in Tyre and elsewhere. (Information in part from CUDL.)

Mercantile letter. In Judaeo-Arabic. On parchment. Dating: 11th century. Refers to coming to Alexandria and staying on the Nile or at sea for 3 days. Refers to 'our colleagues the Maghribī' (aṣḥābnā al-maghāriba). Most of the content is too fragmentary to reconstruct. Various partial names are mentioned (Isḥāq, Abū l-Faraj, Yaʿqūb). On verso, there are greetings to a sister; to Ḥayyim and Hilāl; R. Mardūkh. Mentions Abū l-Faḍl b. Khalfa (potentially the same as in ENA NS 18.35 (PGPID 2441), Umm al-Khayr, and ʿAzrūn. There is a report on prices of commodities (pomegranate, barley, oil) and a br
Legal document in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe (fl. 1100–1138 CE). Fragment. Involves a tenant named Ḥusna, Abū l-Fakhr, and a property.

State document, petition in a chancery hand and large Arabic script. Words that are readily legible include al-Qāhira, al-Ḥāfiẓiyya, al-majlis al-sāmī al-mālikī al-sayyidī al-ajallī al-Afḍalī, al-marsūm. Contains the "rāʾy" clause, "jamīl rāʾy al-majlis al-sāmī". Reused for jottings in Hebrew and Arabic script. On verso there are piyyutim. Needs examination.
Probably the header and poetic Hebrew opening of a letter.
Texts in Judaeo-Arabic, maybe from a letter.

Legal document in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe (fl. 1100–1138 CE) mentioning trade in Yemen and the government. Mentions Maḥfūẓ and Ḥasana. Probably a join with T-S NS 226.107 (PGPID 24248) though it's not clear exactly how (identified by Alan Elbaum).
Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic, one entry lists an amount as a quarter kharrūba. Medieval-era.
Testimony in the hand of Shelomo, dated 1 Tevet 1540 Seleucid which is December 6 1228, about the dissolution of a partnership.
Unidentified literary text in Judaeo-Arabic, mentioning Jonah and the whale and words like "praise" and "the merciful." (Information in part from CUDL.)
List of goods with values, possibly from the trousseau list section of a ketubba.

Recto: Probably a letter fragment in Hebrew. The beginnings of ~5 lines are preserved and several diagonal marginal lines. 

On verso there are accounts in Judaeo-Arabic mentioning copper and an amount owed to R. Aharon.

Recto and verso are both legal drafts, probably in the hand of Shelomo b. Eliyyahu. Verso concerns the same case as in T-S 13J4.4 (PGPID 40402) and contains some identical language. (Information in part from CUDL)

Recto contains Hebrew poetry, likely in the hand of Moshe b. Levi ha-Levi. Verso contains a Judaeo-Arabic letter, likely from Yedutun ha-Levi, in Fustat, to his brother Moshe b. Levi ha-Levi, in Qalyūb. Identifications are based mainly on handwriting. The sender comments on either these or other poems (there are several letters in which Moshe writes that he is enclosing poems and wants feedback on them). There is also something about "mukhāṭabat al-faqīh" here. Yedutun says he might come out and visit on Friday. ASE

Power of attorney. al-Sāliḥ b. Yūsuf, a Sicilian Jew, gives power of attorney to another Jew in a qadi court. Dating: ca. 1102 CE, as the same Ṣāliḥ also appears in T-S NS J95a. On verso there is Hebrew literary text. (Information in part from Goitein’s index card and Khan.)

Letter from a woman to her son Abū ʿAlī Ḥusayn b. Salāma al-Ghurābī(?). In Arabic script. Well preserved and beautifully written. She writes that she has heard about his betrothal (imlāk) to a young woman, and then mentions ʿĪd al-Aḍḥā. She is sick and ailing and urges him to come back lest "the same thing happened as with your father, I won't see you and you won't see me." Needs examination.

Account of burial expenses in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi (fl. 1100–38 CE). It seems to have been a grand funeral with 47 dirhams paid to over a dozen cantors and well over 60 dirhams for all the other expenses, including the transport to the desert, the grave digging, the corpse washing, and camphor and cotton. The cantors and other payees include: Abū Sahl, Ibn al-Kāmukhī, [...] b. Yaʿqūb and his brother, Ibn al-Ḥallāl, Fuhayd, Ibn al-Dhabbāḥ, Maʿālī, al-Ḥayfī, al-Baskhār, Isḥāq Ibn al-Sharābī, Shalom al-Sofer, Yosef, the children of al-Kāmukhī, and ʿImrān. AA/ASE
Probably a fragment from a petition. Possibly two distinct state documents, one each on recto and verso.
Several small fragments. The first is the end of an extremely faded legal document; the singatures of several witnesses are preserved.

Recto (secondary use): In between the lines, in Arabic script, there is a brief recipe for a mulberry syrup containing one ounce each of sugar, mulberry (tūt), blue Egyptian lotus (nūfar), and one other item.

Fragment of a legal record in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe (1100–38 CE). Concerning a family dispute. A woman, Maḥfūẓa from the Ḥātimiyya(?) family, had her inheritance from her father taken by her husband, and domestic strife ensued. In this document, the court orders him not to beat or curse his wife, but rather to honour her and provide her with anything that she was rightfully due. (Information from Goitein's note card and CUDL.)

Letter from Abū l-Surūr b. Ṭarīf to Abū Naṣr b. Yosef. In Judaeo-Arabic. Informing him that Abū l-Najm Hillel had sent him five jars containing qaṭāra (honey with sugar), each weighing about 50 pounds, in the boat of the Rayyis ʿArafāt. (Information from Mediterranean Society, I, p. 463, and from Goitein's index cards.)

IB VII, 42b. Letter from a certain Maḥāsin, in ʿAydhāb, to his "brother" the cantor Abū Isḥāq b. al-Mumḥe, in Fustat. Sent to the shop of Abū l-Munajjā the druggist to be forwarded to the addressee. In Judaeo-Arabic. Begins: "What happened to me would take too long to explain. You will hear it from Abū ʿAlī b. Faḍāʾīl al-Ṣāʾigh (the goldsmith). . . . I am still sitting here in ʿAydhāb, sad and weeping over. . . ." (Information in part from CUDL and Goitein's attached notes.) Dating: probably ca. early 13th century, since the shop of Abū l-Munajjā al-ʿAṭṭār is also the address for T-S Misc.25.2
Letter fragment in Judaeo-Arabic. Faded. Very little substance preserved.

Announcement of a threat of excommunication (ḥerem stam) against anyone in Fustat or Cairo or their environs who knows the whereabouts of Abū l-ʿAlā b. Yosef al-Ṭabīb (the physician) and does not inform the Jewish court. Handwriting of Avraham Maimonides, r. 1205–1237 CE. Verso: jottings with Coptic numerals. (Information in part from CUDL.)
Official receipt of some sort. Needs examination.
Accounts in Arabic and Coptic numerals. Reused for Hebrew pen trials.

Letter in Judaeo-Arabic. The writer asks for a copy of Saadya Gaon's tafsīr of Ezra and Daniel or his tafsīr of Proverbs and Job or one of his commentaries ("parārīsh") on the Torah. He doesn't want it to be like the tafsīr of Psalms, which was written in a lousy hand (ghaliq al-khaṭṭ). The addressee might borrow these books from a friend. The writer's wife and 'mawlā' (father?) send regards. There is a marginal note that ends "if _____, do not send me anything."
Fragment mentioning sums of money, evidently an account.

Letter in Arabic script. Fragment. The writer is giving advice that "perhaps will save you and help you in . . . salvation if God wills." The addressee is to go to a certain zāwiya (Sufi lodge? or simply corner?) and ask for al-Ḥājj Mukhtār al-K[...] (لي والله لاجتهد . . . [ان] شا الله يخلصك ويساعدك في . . . الخلاص انشا الله وتروح الى زاوية صوا . . . وتستصي على الحاج مختار الكـ . . . . الـ . . .). ASE
Small fragment of accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. Probably in the hand of Abū Zikrī Kohen.
Accounts in Hebrew script. Contributors list? There are names in one column and numbers in another. Dating: Probably 16th century. One of the names is Avraham Castro, another is Avraham Ibn Shanji.
Official-looking accounts in Arabic script. Several headers begin "minhā" with an elongated horizontal line. Mentions wheat (qamḥ). Needs examination.
Fragment of a letter mentioning [...] b. ʿAbd al-Karīm. Dating: probably Mamluk-era. (Information in part from CUDL)
Recto: part of a rhymed letter mentioning Yehoshuaʿ (אדוני אבי ריוח והחבר יהושוע). (Information from CUDL)
Recto: Damaged legal document from Fustat. Needs examination.

IB VII, 49. Commercial letter in Judaeo-Arabic, mentioning persons connected with the India trade, including Maḍmūn [b. Ḥasan]. Opens with a report and condolences about the death of a woman. Then the sender orders various garments/textiles according to specifications. (Information in part from CUDL.)
Business letter from Moses Ḥadād to Shim'on Frances in Cairo, with European numerals. Dated Shevat 5567 AM (1807 CE). (Information from CUDL)
Dowry evaluation (taqwīm). Dating: ca. 1200 CE. Lists clothing and jewelry, but no prices. On verso a note in Arabic script and Greek/Coptic numerals. (Information from Goitein's index card.)

Letter, probably from Damascus, in which fifteen elders admonish a community in another country to bring to court a merchant against whom a widow held no fewer then twenty documents of indebtedness. His claims against the orphans of Ibn Saba had to be dealt with separately. Dated 10th century.
Recto: Judaeo-Arabic accounts, mentioning nutmeg (jawza). Verso: Arabic jottings or small fragment of a document. (Information in part from CUDL)
Likely business accounts. In Arabic.
Verso: state document, probably. Part of one line is preserved, referring to "al-abwāb al-sharīfa" and throwing people in jail (الى الابواب الشريفة واعتقلوهم في السجن).
